title: Quran, Sura 70 (al-maʿāriǧ) (Codex Parisino-petropolitanus)
source: Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328) via Gallica IIIF + Corpus Coranicum folio mapping + Tanzil + Pickthall
description: Sura 70 (al-maʿāriǧ) from the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (c. 650-750 AD), one section per folio side, each linked to the exact Gallica image of that page (2 pages).
introduction:
Sura 70 (al-maʿāriǧ) as preserved on 2 folio sides of the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (Paris, BnF Arabe 328 (a) and (b)), one of the oldest surviving Quran manuscripts, written in hijazi script on parchment, c. 650-750 AD. Each section below is one folio side, and the image shown is that exact page.

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side from Gallica (Bibliotheque nationale de France IIIF). The folio's sura:verse range was taken from the Corpus Coranicum "Manuscripta Coranica" record for that page, which states the first and last word on the page; the folio numbers of both services were cross-checked by comparing the two images pixel by pixel.
  2. Original text: the Arabic of the Tanzil Project Uthmani text (CC BY 3.0), reproduced unchanged, verse by verse.
  3. English: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain, verse by verse.

Orthography: the codex is written in scriptio defectiva: no vowel signs, almost no consonantal dots, long vowels often unwritten, and letter shapes that differ from the printed Uthmani text. The modern text given here therefore differs orthographically from what is on the folio while conveying the same reading; readers should expect, for example, the basmala and words such as qala to be spelled with fewer letters on the page.

Numbering: verse numbers follow the standard Kufan (Cairo 1924) division used by Corpus Coranicum, Tanzil and Pickthall. Early codices mark verse ends with ink dots that in places divide the text differently, so a verse count made on the page may not match these numbers exactly. In Tanzil's text the basmala opening each sura (except sura 9) is printed as part of verse 1. Where a page begins or ends in the middle of a verse the whole verse is given and the word position is stated in the section heading.
translator_notes: All 44 verses of this sura are present on the Paris leaves (2 folio sides).
Corpus Coranicum records the first and last word of each page; a verse split across two pages is shown in full under both pages with the word position noted.

translation.original_ref: Quran 70:1-28, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 69v (page ends at word 2 of 70:28; page begins in sura 69 (69:36))
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌۢ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ <sup>2</sup>لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُۥ دَافِعٌ <sup>3</sup>مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذِى ٱلْمَعَارِجِ <sup>4</sup>تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ <sup>5</sup>فَٱصْبِرْ صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا <sup>6</sup>إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُۥ بَعِيدًا <sup>7</sup>وَنَرَىٰهُ قَرِيبًا <sup>8</sup>يَوْمَ تَكُونُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ كَٱلْمُهْلِ <sup>9</sup>وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ <sup>10</sup>وَلَا يَسْـَٔلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا <sup>11</sup>يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِى مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍۭ بِبَنِيهِ <sup>12</sup>وَصَٰحِبَتِهِۦ وَأَخِيهِ <sup>13</sup>وَفَصِيلَتِهِ ٱلَّتِى تُـْٔوِيهِ <sup>14</sup>وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ <sup>15</sup>كَلَّآ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ <sup>16</sup>نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ <sup>17</sup>تَدْعُوا۟ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ <sup>18</sup>وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰٓ <sup>19</sup>إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا <sup>20</sup>إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا <sup>21</sup>وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا <sup>22</sup>إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ <sup>23</sup>ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ <sup>24</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَّعْلُومٌ <sup>25</sup>لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ <sup>26</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ <sup>27</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ <sup>28</sup>إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>A questioner questioned concerning the doom about to fall <sup>2</sup>Upon the disbelievers, which none can repel, <sup>3</sup>From Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways <sup>4</sup>(Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years. <sup>5</sup>But be patient (O Muhammad) with a patience fair to see. <sup>6</sup>Lo! they behold it afar off <sup>7</sup>While we behold it nigh: <sup>8</sup>The day when the sky will become as molten copper, <sup>9</sup>And the hills become as flakes of wool, <sup>10</sup>And no familiar friend will ask a question of his friend <sup>11</sup>Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children <sup>12</sup>And his spouse and his brother <sup>13</sup>And his kin that harboured him <sup>14</sup>And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him. <sup>15</sup>But nay! for lo! it is the fire of hell <sup>16</sup>Eager to roast; <sup>17</sup>It calleth him who turned and fled (from truth), <sup>18</sup>And hoarded (wealth) and withheld it. <sup>19</sup>Lo! man was created anxious, <sup>20</sup>Fretful when evil befalleth him <sup>21</sup>And, when good befalleth him, grudging; <sup>22</sup>Save worshippers. <sup>23</sup>Who are constant at their worship <sup>24</sup>And in whose wealth there is a right acknowledged <sup>25</sup>For the beggar and the destitute; <sup>26</sup>And those who believe in the Day of Judgment, <sup>27</sup>And those who are fearful of their Lord's doom - <sup>28</sup>Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure -

translation.original_ref: Quran 70:28-44, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 70r (page begins at word 4 of 70:28; page continues into sura 71 (71:7))
translation.original_text: <sup>28</sup>إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ <sup>29</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَٰفِظُونَ <sup>30</sup>إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ <sup>31</sup>فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ <sup>32</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَٰعُونَ <sup>33</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِشَهَٰدَٰتِهِمْ قَآئِمُونَ <sup>34</sup>وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ <sup>35</sup>أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍ مُّكْرَمُونَ <sup>36</sup>فَمَالِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ <sup>37</sup>عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ <sup>38</sup>أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ <sup>39</sup>كَلَّآ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُم مِّمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ <sup>40</sup>فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ وَٱلْمَغَٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَٰدِرُونَ <sup>41</sup>عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ <sup>42</sup>فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ <sup>43</sup>يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ <sup>44</sup>خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
translation.text: <sup>28</sup>Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure - <sup>29</sup>And those who preserve their chastity <sup>30</sup>Save with their wives and those whom their right hands possess, for thus they are not blameworthy; <sup>31</sup>But whoso seeketh more than that, those are they who are transgressors; <sup>32</sup>And those who keep their pledges and their covenant, <sup>33</sup>And those who stand by their testimony <sup>34</sup>And those who are attentive at their worship. <sup>35</sup>These will dwell in Gardens, honoured. <sup>36</sup>What aileth those who disbelieve, that they keep staring toward thee (O Muhammad), open-eyed, <sup>37</sup>On the right and on the left, in groups? <sup>38</sup>Doth every man among them hope to enter the Garden of Delight? <sup>39</sup>Nay, verily. Lo! We created them from what they know. <sup>40</sup>But nay! I swear by the Lord of the rising-places and the setting-places of the planets that We verily are Able <sup>41</sup>To replace them by (others) better than them. And we are not to be outrun. <sup>42</sup>So let them chat and play until they meet their Day which they are promised, <sup>43</sup>The day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as racing to a goal, <sup>44</sup>With eyes aghast, abasement stupefying them: Such is the Day which they are promised.
